scenes.line1: Can you ace REST API questions?
scenes.say: Ready to crush REST API interview questions? Do you know which verb does what?

scenes.label: Resource
scenes.sub: A resource is any object, like a user or order, exposed by your API.
scenes.say: In REST, a resource is just an object, like a user or an order, that your API exposes.
The verbs GET, PUT, and DELETE are idempotent. That means repeating them won't change the result. POST is different—run it twice, you might create two things.

scenes.title: Resource & Verb in Action
scenes.say: Here are some classic examples. Get user one two three, post to orders, or put to update a user's email.

scenes.question: Is POST always safe to retry?
scenes.right: Nope! POST is not idempotent. Retrying can create duplicates.
scenes.say: Watch out: POST is not idempotent. If you retry, you could end up with duplicate data.
